topicName: Slow Query Log Analysis and pt-query-digest
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Slow Query Log Analysis and pt-query-digest in MySQL"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Database performance tuning often starts with identifying queries that consume excessive system resources. In MySQL, the Slow Query Log is a powerful diagnostic tool, and Percona Toolkit's pt-query-digest is the industry standard for parsing and summarizing these logs."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Enabling the Slow Query Log"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before analyzing slow queries, you must ensure that logging is enabled in your MySQL instance. You can enable it dynamically without restarting the database server by executing the following SQL commands:"},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"SET GLOBAL slow_query_log = 'ON';\nSET GLOBAL long_query_time = 2;\nSET GLOBAL slow_query_log_file = '/var/log/mysql/mysql-slow.log';"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"slow_query_log = 'ON': Activates the logging mechanism."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"long_query_time = 2: Defines the threshold (in seconds). Any query taking longer than 2 seconds will be recorded."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"slow_query_log_file: Specifies the absolute path where the log file is stored."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Introduction to pt-query-digest"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Raw slow query logs can be massive and difficult to read manually. The pt-query-digest tool reads through these logs, normalizes queries by grouping similar statements together, and generates a comprehensive performance report."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Generating a Standard Report"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"To analyze your log file and output a text-based summary report to your terminal, run the following command:"},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"pt-query-digest /var/log/mysql/mysql-slow.log > slow_query_report.txt"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"This creates a report containing an overall summary, a profile of all executed queries ranked by total execution time, and detailed breakdowns of the most problematic queries."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Analyzing the Report Sections"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Overall Summary: Shows metrics like total query execution time, unique queries, and response time distributions."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Query Profile: Lists queries ranked by metrics such as rank, ID, response time, calls, and items per query."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Query Detail: Provides deep-dive statistics for individual query fingerprints, including EXPLAIN plans and execution frequency charts."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 5: Advanced Usage Scenarios"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can use pt-query-digest to capture queries directly from the network interface in real-time if you cannot wait for file-based logging:"},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"pt-query-digest --type=tcpdump --limit=10"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Alternatively, to review only queries executed against a specific database user or host, you can integrate standard Linux utilities or filter flags provided by the toolkit."}]
